# Foundation 0.1.0 release readiness

**NOT READY**. Run `./scripts/inventory readiness` for every missing obligation and identity diagnostic. Inventory validity is separate from release readiness; regular `verify` checks the current contract without certifying it.

Authorities: [obligations](../../capabilities/foundation-release.yaml), [source requirements](../../capabilities/foundation-requirements.yaml), [environment profiles](../../capabilities/foundation-environments.yaml), [retained evidence](../../capabilities/foundation-evidence.yaml).

Only actually exercised Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux x86-64 environments with JDK 8, 11, 17 and 21 are required. **Windows x86-64 and macOS x86-64/arm64 are uncertified and are not required release gates for Foundation 0.1.0.** [ADR-0040](../../docs/adr/0040-certify-only-observed-foundation-environments.md) supersedes only ADR-0026's platform requirement for this version. All other Foundation requirements remain mandatory. Matching architecture names or JDK majors never extend certification.

## Retained limitations

Classifications bind the exact Capability Matrix limitation text by SHA-256; changed or unclassified text fails inventory validation. A release-blocker must be resolved by its owning slice, with preserved source requirements and evidence; deleting required behavior is not a resolution.

- `document.blank.create-publish-reopen` / `retained-contract` → [`transactions`](#transactions): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #70 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T15 supplies revision-preserving INCREMENTAL publication through this transaction seam; INCREMENTAL requires an existing primary Source and applies a closed command policy.
- `document.blank.create-publish-reopen` / `retained-contract` → [`transactions`](#transactions): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #70 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T15 separately recognizes Existing Signatures, rejects signed REWRITE publication, and conservatively authorizes signed incremental changes from DocMDP evidence.
- `document.blank.create-publish-reopen` / `retained-contract` → [`transactions`](#transactions): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #70 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T03 opens only the explicitly selected primary source unless an ordered Document Command, such as T10 merge, explicitly selects additional named Sources.
- `document.blank.create-publish-reopen` / `retained-contract` → [`transactions`](#transactions): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #70 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T20 layers finite-default transaction-wide resource accounting and cooperative checkpoints onto T03. T21 separately supplies an opt-in isolated Worker with hard Worker termination; the caller callback intentionally remains in the caller process.
- `document.value.inspect-patch` / `retained-contract` → [`values`](#values): Required ordered dictionary, array, value and stream edits are implemented through both public interfaces; preserving valid core structure and separate downstream feature policies remains the low-level contract.
  Original limitation: Patch version 2 supports ordered dictionary set/remove, array set/insert/remove, value replacement and stream data replacement through nested paths; existing dictionary-only version-1 requests retain their representation. Low-level Patches must preserve valid core structure and do not grant downstream feature semantics.
- `document.value.inspect-patch` / `retained-contract` → [`values`](#values): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #71 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Unsigned REWRITE and INCREMENTAL preserve Source bytes and existing indirect identity. Existing Signatures authorize no DocumentPatch; version and password-security state remain owned by their explicit output policies.
- `document.value.inspect-patch` / `retained-contract` → [`values`](#values): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #71 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Inspection uses bounded Session views. Native query limits are explicit; the Facade uses 100000 traversed values and 64 MiB cumulative decoded bytes per inspection. Workflow resource exhaustion is terminal; ordinary Patch and inspection-limit failures remain recoverable. Backend materialization has a finite 256-level depth bound before recursive conversion.
- `document.value.inspect-patch` / `retained-contract` → [`values`](#values): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #71 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Native IN_PROCESS and HARDENED_WORKER share the closed value and versioned Patch codecs. The mapped Facade owns one IN_PROCESS Native Session per Document, uses REWRITE publication, and preserves caller-owned streams; Native execution and policy controls are not Facade mappings.
- `document.value.inspect-patch` / `retained-contract` → [`values`](#values): Decoded stream replacement supports explicit unfiltered and Flate output with atomic engine-owned metadata; untouched encoded streams and unknown resources retain their bytes, attributes and references.
  Original limitation: Stream replacements accept decoded bytes with explicit unfiltered or Flate encoding; Length, Filter, DecodeParms and external-file metadata remain engine-owned. Untouched encoded bytes, unknown resources and attributes are preserved; unknown decoding fails safely and external-file streams are never resolved.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): T72 public Native and Facade contracts plus candidate-bound T10 evidence retain this requirement while covering all required successful Foundation page cases.
  Original limitation: T15 admits T10 primary-document commands for unsigned INCREMENTAL publication but rejects SplitDocument; Existing Signatures authorize no T10 command in version 1.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): The fixed T10 corpus exercises every required successful Foundation page operation; conservative page-graph rejection remains the documented safe-failure boundary.
  Original limitation: Page operations preserve tested inherited boxes, rotation, resources, content, the legacy basic Text-annotation dictionary key set, and managed T12 annotations and local GoTo Action bindings when copied or reparented; only required NM collision renaming and P page retargeting change a copied legacy annotation. Before mutation, T10 rejects nonstructural trailer data, nonempty document information, catalogs or page-tree nodes with unproven entries, inconsistent page-tree parents, counts, cycles, repeated nodes, or any direct input page-tree node, missing effective media boxes, malformed box, rotation, or resource entries, resource graphs that reach page or page-tree structures, nested content arrays, external-file content streams, filtered content streams unless they use one parameter-free FlateDecode or Fl filter with a strictly valid zlib payload, content streams with non-engine metadata, unproven indirect page extensions, separation information, unsupported annotation relationships or Action graphs, tagged-page references, and thread beads. Managed document information, XMP metadata, outlines, named destinations, and embedded files are validated, preserved, and retargeted by the document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments capability; managed annotations and Actions are validated, preserved, and retargeted by document.annotations-actions.manage; forms and tagged structure remain downstream capability slices.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): T72 public Native and Facade contracts plus candidate-bound T10 evidence retain this requirement while covering all required successful Foundation page cases.
  Original limitation: Copy, merge, and split preserve semantic page graphs, not source byte layout or backend object identity. Object References are Session-local; public reopen-and-rewrite probes demonstrate that changing an imported content graph leaves its Source and sibling products unchanged.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): T72 public Native and Facade contracts plus candidate-bound T10 evidence retain this requirement while covering all required successful Foundation page cases.
  Original limitation: T10 validates command ranges, positions, named merge Sources, and exact split Target coverage. A successful SplitDocument is terminal for Document Commands in that workflow; its local limits compose with T20's transaction-wide page, object, nesting, decompression, memory, time, storage, input, pixel, and concurrency policy.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): T72 public Native and Facade contracts plus candidate-bound T10 evidence retain this requirement while covering all required successful Foundation page cases.
  Original limitation: T10 runs through the trusted in-process adapter by default; T21's opt-in Hardened Worker transports the same page, merge, and split commands and queries through closed version-1 codecs.
- `document.page.manipulate-merge-split` / `retained-contract` → [`pages`](#pages): T72 public Native and Facade contracts plus candidate-bound T10 evidence retain this requirement while covering all required successful Foundation page cases.
  Original limitation: A new split product that has no trailer identifier receives one derived from a fixed-placeholder serialization of that product; existing identifiers and non-split publication are unchanged. T10 makes no broader source-byte-layout guarantee.
- `document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments` / `retained-contract` → [`metadata`](#metadata): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #73 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T15 admits T11 commands for unsigned INCREMENTAL publication; Existing Signatures authorize no T11 command in version 1.
- `document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments` / `retained-contract` → [`metadata`](#metadata): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #73 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Outlines are written all-open with positive visible-item counts, and name trees are written as one flat array sorted by unsigned encoded key-byte order; richer tree shapes are read only when they satisfy the proven safe invariants, and are otherwise preserved intact or rejected with PRESERVATION_UNSUPPORTED.
- `document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments` / `retained-contract` → [`metadata`](#metadata): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #73 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: A page removal that would orphan a managed destination fails with DESTINATION_CONFLICT before mutation; destinations that target pages outside a split selection are dropped from that product, and merge renames colliding destination and embedded-file names with a deterministic -N suffix.
- `document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments` / `retained-contract` → [`metadata`](#metadata): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #73 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Inspection and payload bounds are explicit per-query limits failing with METADATA_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; XMP command packets must be well-formed XML carrying the XMP root marker within a 64 MiB bound, and embedded-file MIME subtypes are restricted to printable ASCII. These local bounds compose with T20's transaction policy and are transported by T21's opt-in Hardened Worker codecs.
- `document.metadata.outlines-destinations-attachments` / `retained-contract` → [`metadata`](#metadata): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #73 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Managed annotations and local GoTo Actions integrate through document.annotations-actions.manage; content extraction remains T13 and T14, and encryption remains T16.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `retained-contract` → [`annotations`](#annotations): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #74 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: T15 admits all T12 commands for unsigned INCREMENTAL publication; a sole coherent DocMDP P=3 policy admits only supported non-Widget UpdateAnnotations changes, while UpdateActions and FlattenAnnotations remain rejected for signed Sources.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `release-blocker` → [`annotations`](#annotations): The Foundation annotation subset and deferred AcroForm boundary require #74 reconciliation.
  Original limitation: Version 1 manages Text, Stamp, Highlight, FileAttachment, standalone Widget, and Link annotations. Widget values do not create AcroForm fields and cannot be flattened; AcroForm field behavior, form Actions, and form flattening remain outside T12.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `release-blocker` → [`annotations`](#annotations): The GoTo allowlist must cover the required Foundation Action subset under #74.
  Original limitation: The complete Action allowlist is an inert local GoTo dictionary with one direct page or existing named-destination target, bound only to catalog open, page open or close, and Link annotations. Folio PDF never executes Actions; unsupported or chained Action graphs remain structurally unchanged only during rewrites that need not interpret them and are otherwise rejected before mutation. Source-byte preservation is not claimed.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `release-blocker` → [`annotations`](#annotations): Restricted appearance/flattening support must cover the required Foundation annotation behavior under #74.
  Original limitation: Normal appearances are resource-free Form XObjects with an identity matrix, an empty Resources dictionary, a 1 MiB decoded-content limit, semantically range-checked graphics operands, and a strict operator allowlist. Flattening requires a validated normal appearance, isolates pre-existing page content with q/Q, and supports non-Widget annotations only.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `retained-contract` → [`annotations`](#annotations): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #74 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Annotation counts, appearance bytes, and attachment bytes are caller-bounded on query. Each complete managed-graph command or page-operation validation or retargeting pass shares fixed document-wide 8 MiB decoded-appearance and 8 MiB decoded-attachment bounds. These local bounds compose with T20's shared transaction policy and are transported by T21's opt-in Hardened Worker codecs.
- `document.annotations-actions.manage` / `retained-contract` → [`annotations`](#annotations): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #74 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Copy, merge, and split classify each annotation-array entry independently, preserve proven-safe legacy basic Text annotations alongside managed entries in either order, retarget supported direct and named destinations by page identity, deterministically suffix colliding annotation identifiers including an optional legacy identifier on a copied Text entry, reject unrenamable legacy identifier collisions before merge target mutation, and filter bindings whose target does not survive a split. Removing a named destination fails atomically with DESTINATION_CONFLICT while a managed Link or Action still refers to it. Source-byte layout and cross-Session object identity are not claimed.
- `document.text-structure.extract` / `retained-contract` → [`text`](#text): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #75 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Version 1 returns page-tree and content-stream execution order, including Form invocation order. Contents arrays are parsed as one newline-separated stream and may split tokens across members. Version 1 does not infer visual or semantic reading order, whitespace, line breaks, columns, paragraphs, bidi order, OCR, or layout.
- `document.text-structure.extract` / `retained-contract` → [`text`](#text): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #75 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Character evidence uses independently parsed ToUnicode mappings and explicitly declared simple-font Differences entries for exact codes, otherwise falling back only to a recognized Encoding or BaseEncoding, all mapped through the public Adobe Glyph List. An absent or unknown base supplies no unoverridden mapping. Composite fonts without ToUnicode, font programs, substituted or system fonts, renderers, and backend coercions are never promoted to confident Unicode.
- `document.text-structure.extract` / `release-blocker` → [`text`](#text): Required Logical Structure extraction must be reconciled with the restricted MCR/OBJR/PDF 2.0 profiles by #75.
  Original limitation: Marked-content ActualText replaces enclosed aggregate Page Text once with outer replacement precedence, while Alt remains separate. Logical structure uses iterative depth-bounded traversal and supports ordered nested elements, direct page MCIDs and explicit page-content MCR dictionaries, optional StructElem Type values, transitive unqualified RoleMap resolution to the PDF 1.7 standard-role vocabulary, and element-ancestor-catalog language inheritance. Unqualified PDF 2.0-only roles remain unresolved. Elements are visited once and must carry the parent backlink implied by K; repeated/shared elements, inconsistent parents, marked content inside Form XObjects, MCRs carrying Stm or StmOwn, OBJR children, and PDF 2.0 structure namespaces fail safely outside version 1.

A batch made only of AddBlankPage, InsertBlankPage, CopyPages, MovePages, and RemovePages is eligible for an encoded-length offer while its complete modeled transport peak fits the parent's current message and aggregate owned-memory bounds. That peak is the larger of growable encoder capacity plus retained payload and simultaneous parent/child payload ownership plus the retained/received completion control. It crosses in one atomic frame only when the Worker accepts its current modeled-memory cost. Every other, parent-ineligible, or Worker-deferred batch sends one authenticated declaration fixing the complete ordered count, then sends each indexed preflight, required detail, and Command only when the Worker requests it after its predecessor succeeds. Both forms receive one logical completion. Encoding or materializing later staged Commands is deferred, so execution stops at the first failure without consuming later one-shot inputs or allowing a later resource failure to replace an earlier semantic or backend failure. Execute delegates its singleton batch through the same selection, and each Query is a synchronous ordering barrier. Lazy PDF Value views use bounded authenticated operations, remain serviceable while the Worker awaits a deferred item so they can be used by a later Command, and expire with their proxy Session. Nested PDF Value, outline, and logical-structure codecs are iterative through the public version-1 nesting ceiling. At the T21 fixed point each value fit one configured message; the separate T22 recovery-and-scale capability adds bounded authenticated chunking.

The Worker receives only random local handles; the parent retains actual Targets and caller-owned streams or channels and publishes only after a valid finished response and confirmed Worker exit. Reference Font Set entries and explicit Font Sources remain parent-owned and unopened until selected. The selecting Command applies declaration and source-count checks and carries opaque identifiers; the Worker requests each program in declaration order, and the parent applies the aggregate-byte, first-excess, and one-shot reuse rules before returning it in a separate bounded frame. Committed Worker products remain cumulatively charged to the shared temporary-storage ceiling. Existing Save Mode, receipt, partial-stream, replacement, and Provider-selection contracts remain authoritative.

Before every nonempty parent-to-child application frame, the parent reserves and grants its exact payload allocation; the child reserves and releases other decoded or retained allocations through authenticated memory controls; and each quiescent response is followed by an acknowledged empty memory synchronization before the next parent allocation. Atomic-batch eligibility includes the larger of the parent's growable encoder plus retained-payload peak and simultaneous parent/child payload ownership plus the retained/received completion control. Active-context application payloads, decoded String/byte copies, conservatively charged collection capacity, credentials, and normal failure envelopes are cleared or released at their actual lifetime boundaries without sampling the caller Clock on the reader thread. Fixed 12-byte authenticated memory reserve, release, and grant payloads are the sole active control-plane exception and remain outside the ledger to prevent recursive accounting while retaining pre-allocation message-bound checks. Pre-context and post-context failures use a fixed eight-byte allowlisted descriptor, and the fixed eight-byte post-context FINISHED control contains only a version and allowlisted capability token, because no transaction ledger is live. Counts are checked against remaining wire bytes and charged before capacity-bearing allocation. The bootstrap decoder applies the parent-supplied memory ceiling before the child context exists, and decoded initialization collection capacity remains charged for the active transaction after READY; the fixed failure codec remains available as an emergency only when the primary failure has already poisoned or exhausted an active context.

Count exhaustion or an oversized envelope rejects a new identity before callback or publication; an oversized pre-admission declaration creates no status and may omit receipts rather than copying over-limit metadata. Because caller callback meaning and mutable Path contents cannot be fingerprinted, the application must preserve their logical meaning across a recoverable retry and must restore the same caller-owned Source stream or channel to its original readable position; an unrepeatable one-shot Source is unsuitable for retry. Exhaustion is COMPOSITION_AREA_EXHAUSTED, invalid declarations are COMPOSITION_INVALID, and composition bounds use COMPOSITION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; dependency failures retain their codes and safe diagnostics.

An explicit area break conflicts with a pending keep. A final keep is vacuous.

Arbitrary affine geometry does not certify physical scanning or page fit.

- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `retained-contract` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #95 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.

The caller does not select a mask. DataMatrix supports AUTO, ASCII, C40, TEXT, X12, EDIFACT, BASE256 and validated RAW data; ECC200 correction follows the selected square or rectangular size. Each dimension can be fixed or automatic. Measurement performs bounded encoding and returns detached matrix and full point dimensions without painting or requiring a page.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `retained-contract` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #95 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.

No trimming, normalization, escape-string interpretation or implicit charset fallback occurs. ECI-ignoring scanners are outside the claim.

Reader programming cannot combine with FNC1; Macro cannot combine with sequence or reader programming; RAW cannot also carry typed headers or text encoding. AUTO Macro with FNC1 or nondefault ECI uses ASCII compaction. Raw controls must be supported, complete and end in ASCII state; caller padding and ECC are rejected.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `release-blocker` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): Every Reference Suite PDF417 generation mode must be reconciled under #95; raster-only inversion and other exclusions cannot hide required vector modes.
  Original limitation: PDF417 supports automatic text/numeric/byte compaction, forced BINARY, validated RAW and typed Macro including one segment. ECC is automatic or exactly 0–8; columns are 1–30, rows 3–90 and total codewords at most 928. Zero dimensions select automatically; a fixed rectangle never silently changes. Positive aspect ratio is physical matrix height/width excluding quiet margins and is exclusive of fixed rows/columns. Macro file IDs are numeric triplets 000–899, segment indices are zero-based and counts are 1–99999. Raw embedded Macro controls are rejected; typed Macro remains available with RAW. No automatic file splitting/assembly, MicroPDF417, truncated PDF417 or bitmap inversion API is provided.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `retained-contract` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #95 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.

Equivalent local vectors and boxes reuse indirect Forms across pages. Arbitrary finite nondegenerate affine placement is admitted within Canvas bounds; page fit, existing ink, contrast and physical scanning remain caller concerns.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `retained-contract` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #95 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.
  Original limitation: Declaration bounds are 8192 UTF-16 units or raw words, a 32-character encoding name and a 2700-character Macro file ID, in addition to family capacities. Encoding reserves 8 MiB of modeled owned memory, vectors are bounded at 4 MiB and placements at 512 bytes; cache and existing Workflow resource accounting remain effective. Stable checked mode/input/geometry/limit failures preserve publication targets and safe diagnostics. No image-pixel allowance is needed.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `retained-contract` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): This preserves the explicit ownership, bounded execution, representation or safe-preservation contract; #95 must prove it without omitting required successful Foundation cases.

Existing permissions, signature protection, unsigned incremental behavior and publication contracts apply. Encoder state is Session-owned; decoder algorithms, charset SPI and external tools stay in tests or the non-distributed acceptance module.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `release-blocker` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): The complete 224-page-per-mode corpus and damaged controls need final candidate/environment evidence under #95.

Independent assertions consume reopened public PDF Values and actual rasters. Nineteen damaged public PDFs must fail semantic and raster checks and differ visually, including wrong padding with independently recomputed ECC.
- `composition.barcodes.two-dimensional` / `release-blocker` → [`barcodes-2d`](#barcodes-2d): Independent standards, compatible dependencies, required environments and 2D Facade remain incomplete.
  Original limitation: Independent PDF standards certification, compatible-status dependencies and Foundation platform certification remain open. Passing decoding, qpdf and visual checks does not grant compatible status, a Migration Facade mapping or T33 release certification.

## Source requirement catalogue

<a id="spec-us-01"></a>
- `spec-us-01` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 1
  As a Java 8 application developer, I want artifacts that genuinely run on Java 8, so that I can migrate without upgrading my production JVM.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

- `spec-us-02` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 2
  As a developer on a later JDK, I want the same artifacts tested on JDK 11, 17, and 21, so that runtime upgrades do not require a different library line.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-us-71"></a>
- `spec-us-71` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 71
  As a user, I want authoritative English specifications and a Chinese usage guide, so that contracts remain consistent while Chinese-speaking users have practical documentation.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-us-72"></a>
- `spec-us-72` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 72
  As a project maintainer, I want public non-affiliation notices, so that Folio PDF by ZeroCloud is not confused with LibrePDF OpenPDF or Apryse iText.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-us-73"></a>
- `spec-us-73` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 73
  As a server operator, I want acceptance at approximately 5,000 pages and 1 GiB with controlled spill, so that large bounded workloads are supported without promising unlimited streaming.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `recovery`

<a id="spec-us-74"></a>
- `spec-us-74` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 74
  As a privacy reviewer, I want logs to omit filenames, content, metadata, credentials, private keys, and raw backend exceptions, so that operational visibility does not leak sensitive data.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions, worker, providers`

<a id="spec-us-75"></a>
- `spec-us-75` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — User Stories 75
  As a community member, I want contributors to retain copyright under DCO and Apache-2.0 inbound terms, so that participation does not require copyright assignment.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `provenance`

<a id="spec-id-01"></a>
- `spec-id-01` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 1
  The fixed Reference Suite is iText Core 7.2.6, pdfSweep 3.0.2, pdfCalligraph 3.0.2, pdfXFA 3.0.4, pdfHTML 4.0.5, pdfOCR 2.0.2, pdfOptimizer 2.0.2, pdfRender 2.0.4, and pdfOffice 2.0.5.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-id-02"></a>
- `spec-id-02` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 2
  Capability Parity means supported counterparts for the fixed suite. It excludes unchanged imports, binary linkage, byte-identical output, identical backend exceptions, and an automatically moving target.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs, acceptance`

<a id="spec-id-03"></a>
- `spec-id-03` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 3
  Implementation is clean-room and Apache-2.0. iText source and resources may not be copied or adapted, and closed add-ons may not be reverse-engineered.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `provenance`

<a id="spec-id-04"></a>
- `spec-id-04` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 4
  Public standards, public API documentation, project-owned fixtures, and legally approved black-box evidence are allowed. Standards remain the correctness authority.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `provenance, acceptance`

<a id="spec-id-05"></a>
- `spec-id-05` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 5
  The public identity is Folio PDF by ZeroCloud. Java packages use net.zerocloud.pdf and artifacts use net.zerocloud:pdf-*.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs, java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-06"></a>
- `spec-id-06` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 6
  The canonical public repository and issue tracker are zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf. GitHub Issues use the default needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, and wontfix vocabulary.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-id-07"></a>
- `spec-id-07` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 7
  Java 8 is a runtime contract. Maven builds use a Java-8-compatible Maven 3.9 release and compile with release 8; tests run on JDK 8, 11, 17, and 21.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-08"></a>
- `spec-id-08` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 8
  All first-party 0.x artifacts share one Release Train managed by pdf-bom. Unimplemented placeholder artifacts are not published.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-09"></a>
- `spec-id-09` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 9
  Deep modules are organized around Document Engine, Composition, Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion, Sanitization, and Migration rather than copying Reference Suite packaging.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-10"></a>
- `spec-id-10` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 10
  The first-party artifact families are pdf-bom, pdf-document, pdf-composition, pdf-forms, pdf-trust, pdf-conformance, pdf-conversion, pdf-sanitization, pdf-migration-itext7, pdf-provider-*, pdf-acceptance, and pdf-testkit.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-11"></a>
- `spec-id-11` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 11
  Capability dependency cycles are forbidden. Acceptance and test artifacts never enter production runtime.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts, integration`

<a id="spec-id-12"></a>
- `spec-id-12` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 12
  The Native Interface is centered on DocumentWorkflow.execute with a caller-side Document Work callback and a thread-confined Document Session.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-13"></a>
- `spec-id-13` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 13
  A Workflow Request contains named sources, a primary source, named publication targets, Save Mode, execution policy, resource limits, credentials, and provider preferences.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-14"></a>
- `spec-id-14` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 14
  A Workflow Outcome contains the caller result, capability and execution information, safe diagnostics, and per-target Publication Receipts.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-15"></a>
- `spec-id-15` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 15
  The callback always runs in the caller process, including under the Hardened Worker Profile. Workers never receive lambdas or user bytecode.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker`

<a id="spec-id-16"></a>
- `spec-id-16` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 16
  Document Commands are project-defined, versioned, ordered, batchable mutation values. Document Queries are project-defined ordering barriers that observe all prior Commands.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker, transactions`

<a id="spec-id-17"></a>
- `spec-id-17` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 17
  Arbitrary user implementations, Java Serialization, reflection class names, scripts, arbitrary URIs, and backend objects are rejected at the execution boundary.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker, values`

<a id="spec-id-18"></a>
- `spec-id-18` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 18
  The core API is synchronous. Deadlines, cancellation tokens, and sanitized progress events are explicit; callers may use their own Executor for asynchronous composition.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-19"></a>
- `spec-id-19` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 19
  The Workflow Environment is immutable and thread-safe and owns provider registrations, command/query codecs, reference fonts, temporary storage, worker launch, Clock, Locale, time zone, SecureRandom, and default policy.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions, providers, fonts, worker`

<a id="spec-id-20"></a>
- `spec-id-20` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 20
  There are no implicit system fonts, default Locale, default time zone, or network calls in compatibility evidence.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `acceptance, fonts, paragraphs`

<a id="spec-id-21"></a>
- `spec-id-21` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 21
  The Document Engine owns a backend-neutral PDF Value model covering null, boolean, number, string, name, array, dictionary, stream, and indirect reference.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `values`

<a id="spec-id-22"></a>
- `spec-id-22` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 22
  Small values may be immutable and detached. Large streams and traversals are bounded lazy Session views addressed by Object References and invalid after Session close.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `values`

<a id="spec-id-23"></a>
- `spec-id-23` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 23
  Low-level changes use validated Document Patches. PDFBox COS and PD types are never public contracts.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `values, java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-24"></a>
- `spec-id-24` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 24
  REWRITE and INCREMENTAL are explicit Save Modes. Unsigned ordinary edits default to REWRITE.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions, incremental`

<a id="spec-id-25"></a>
- `spec-id-25` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 25
  Signed files are read-only by default. Only proven permitted changes may use explicit incremental publication.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `incremental`

<a id="spec-id-26"></a>
- `spec-id-26` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 26
  Unknown content and resources are preserved when safe; the operation fails when safe preservation cannot be guaranteed.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `values, pages, metadata, annotations`

<a id="spec-id-27"></a>
- `spec-id-27` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 27
  Path inputs opened by the module are closed by the module. Caller-provided streams and channels remain caller-owned. Byte and Worker inputs are copied or staged under limits.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-28"></a>
- `spec-id-28` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 28
  All products are staged and validated before publication. Path targets use atomic replacement where supported. Stream failures report possible partial output. There is no global transaction across multiple targets.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-29"></a>
- `spec-id-29` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 29
  Document Failure is a checked operational contract with stable codes, capability identifiers, and safe diagnostics. Programming errors remain unchecked, while caller runtime exceptions abort and propagate unchanged.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `transactions`

<a id="spec-id-30"></a>
- `spec-id-30` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 30
  The same Native Interface supports In-Process and Hardened Worker execution. Hostile multi-tenant input requires the Worker.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker`

<a id="spec-id-31"></a>
- `spec-id-31` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 31
  The first Worker is a local-only child process with a versioned, authenticated, length-bounded protocol, transaction IDs, deadlines, checksums, bounded chunking or staging, and crash recovery.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker, recovery`

<a id="spec-id-32"></a>
- `spec-id-32` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 32
  Each Worker transaction uses a private restricted temporary root. Worker networking is disabled; remote providers are brokered by the parent and require explicit disclosure consent.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker, providers`

<a id="spec-id-33"></a>
- `spec-id-33` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 33
  The default Foundation backend is PDFBox 3.0.8, hidden inside pdf-document. No public backend SPI or API/implementation artifact split is introduced until a second real backend exists.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-34"></a>
- `spec-id-34` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 34
  ICU4J 77.1 handles Unicode segmentation, bidi, script and line-break behavior; it is not treated as a shaping engine.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `paragraphs`

<a id="spec-id-35"></a>
- `spec-id-35` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 35
  OkapiBarcode 0.5.6 is the default encoder, with project-owned PDF vector rendering for all Reference Suite barcode modes.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `barcodes-1d, barcodes-2d`

<a id="spec-id-36"></a>
- `spec-id-36` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 36
  TwelveMonkeys is optional and used only where additional image decoding is required after license review.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `graphics, supply-chain`

<a id="spec-id-37"></a>
- `spec-id-37` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 37
  High-level layout, pagination, tables, font fallback, shaping orchestration, hyphenation, resource reuse, image policy, and color policy are owned by Folio PDF.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `canvas, graphics, fonts, paragraphs, pagination, tables, shaping`

<a id="spec-id-38"></a>
- `spec-id-38` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 38
  Complex shaping uses a project-owned HarfBuzz native adapter. HarfBuzz is not bundled and is certified on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS x86-64, and macOS arm64.
  Disposition: `required`. Only the four-platform portion is superseded by ADR-0040/#69; all typography, reference-font, native and independent-evidence requirements remain mandatory on the required Ubuntu/JDK profiles. Obligations: `environments, shaping`

<a id="spec-id-39"></a>
- `spec-id-39` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 39
  Typography evidence uses hash-pinned static Noto Sans, CJK SC/TC/JP/KR, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, and Thai fonts with OFL notices. System and online fonts are not evidence inputs.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `fonts, paragraphs, shaping, provenance`

<a id="spec-id-40"></a>
- `spec-id-40` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 40
  Foundation reads PDF 1.0 through 2.0 and supported legacy password encryption, writes PDF 1.7 with AES-256 by default, and supports explicit PDF 2.0 output.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `password-baseline`

<a id="spec-id-41"></a>
- `spec-id-41` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 41
  Obsolete output algorithms require Legacy Security Mode.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `password-baseline`

<a id="spec-id-42"></a>
- `spec-id-42` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 42
  Foundation recognizes and protects existing signatures but does not create or validate them.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `incremental`

<a id="spec-id-43"></a>
- `spec-id-43` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 43
  Public-key encryption, signatures, certificate chains, external signing, HSM, TSA, OCSP, CRL, DSS, LTV, and PAdES belong to the later Trust module.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-44"></a>
- `spec-id-44` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 44
  Foundation makes no FIPS claim. A future FIPS Distribution must pin a certified provider, JVM, platform, startup mode, and evidence, with no normal-provider coexistence or fallback.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-id-45"></a>
- `spec-id-45` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 45
  The Reference Conformance Set is PDF/A-1A/1B, PDF/A-2A/2B/2U, PDF/A-3A/3B/3U, and tagged plus metadata-assisted PDF/UA-1 creation.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-46"></a>
- `spec-id-46` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 46
  Creation Checks and Independent Validation are separate concepts. PDF/A-4, PDF/UA-2, and a public PDF/UA validator are not part of the fixed baseline.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `acceptance, docs`

<a id="spec-id-47"></a>
- `spec-id-47` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 47
  Conversion uses replaceable Capability Providers with project-owned requests and results. Providers declare execution mode, engine version, license and distribution facts, availability, and limits.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `providers`

<a id="spec-id-48"></a>
- `spec-id-48` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 48
  The initial OCR provider is Tesseract CLI. Core rendering and searchable text-layer construction remain owned by Folio PDF.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-49"></a>
- `spec-id-49` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 49
  The default runtime renderer is PDFBox Renderer. Independent PDFium rendering is used for visual acceptance.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `rendering, acceptance`

<a id="spec-id-50"></a>
- `spec-id-50` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 50
  The initial Office provider is a user-installed LibreOffice headless CLI. LibreOffice is not bundled, and fidelity is judged through pinned acceptance corpora.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-51"></a>
- `spec-id-51` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 51
  Sanitization must remove underlying content; overlays and annotations do not count as secure redaction.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-52"></a>
- `spec-id-52` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 52
  The Migration Facade keeps reference package suffixes beneath net.zerocloud.pdf.itext7 and lowers migration cost without preserving imports or linkage.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `facade-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-53"></a>
- `spec-id-53` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 53
  pdf-migration-itext7 contains only compatible mappings. pdf-migration-itext7-preview is a mutually exclusive superset containing compatible and experimental mappings.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `facade-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-54"></a>
- `spec-id-54` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 54
  The project does not publish a complete surface made of unsupported runtime-throwing stubs.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `facade-artifacts, java-artifacts`

<a id="spec-id-55"></a>
- `spec-id-55` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 55
  capability-matrix.yaml is the behavioral authority. facade-surface.yaml is the source-surface authority. Generated documentation links them in both directions.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `docs`

<a id="spec-id-56"></a>
- `spec-id-56` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 56
  Capability states are planned, experimental, compatible, and limited. Compatible requires complete Acceptance Evidence.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `integration, acceptance`

<a id="spec-id-57"></a>
- `spec-id-57` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 57
  During 0.x, public source-breaking changes require migration notes. From 1.0, semantic versioning governs public compatibility.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `java-artifacts, docs`

<a id="spec-id-58"></a>
- `spec-id-58` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 58
  Foundation Release 0.1.0 includes Document Engine, the complete Foundation Composition Profile, page rendering, password encryption, existing-signature protection, matching Stable Migration Facade coverage, hostile-input handling, and acceptance infrastructure.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `integration`

<a id="spec-id-59"></a>
- `spec-id-59` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 59
  Remaining Core work opens Forms, Trust, Conformance, SVG, and styled XML after verified prerequisites.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-60"></a>
- `spec-id-60` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 60
  Sanitization, optimization, OCR, and XFA may proceed in parallel after their own Dependency Gates.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-61"></a>
- `spec-id-61` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 61
  HTML conversion requires compatible Forms, Layout, SVG, and styled XML; advanced scripts additionally require shaping.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-62"></a>
- `spec-id-62` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 62
  Office conversion is last in the current advisory order because it benefits from mature layout, typography, image, and rendering evidence.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none

<a id="spec-id-63"></a>
- `spec-id-63` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 63
  The project uses Apache-2.0, DCO, contributor provenance, no copyright assignment, and the notice identity Folio PDF by ZeroCloud contributors.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `provenance`

<a id="spec-id-64"></a>
- `spec-id-64` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 64
  The Lead Maintainer is initially the project founder under ZeroCloud SDK. The temporary public and security contact is mabaiqiu@gmail.com.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `supply-chain`

<a id="spec-id-65"></a>
- `spec-id-65` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Implementation Decisions 65

<a id="spec-id-69"></a>

<a id="spec-id-70"></a>

<a id="spec-td-01"></a>
- `spec-td-01` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 1
  The highest and primary test seam is observable behavior through DocumentWorkflow.execute. Tests supply public requests, Commands and Queries and assert outcomes, Publication Receipts, files, stable failures, resource ownership, and lifecycle behavior.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `integration`

<a id="spec-td-02"></a>
- `spec-td-02` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 2
  In-Process and Hardened Worker adapters run the same Document Workflow contract suite. Worker tests add batching, query barriers, protocol compatibility, timeouts, cancellation, crash recovery, uncertain commit lookup, malformed messages, and resource-limit enforcement.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `worker, recovery, integration`

<a id="spec-td-03"></a>
- `spec-td-03` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 3
  The Migration Facade is tested at its public surface by invoking mapped behavior and asserting the same Native Interface outcomes. Tests do not assert internal delegation classes.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `facade-artifacts`

<a id="spec-td-04"></a>
- `spec-td-04` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 4
  Provider-specific contract tests exist only at real external Capability Provider seams. PDFBox, ICU4J, OkapiBarcode, and ordinary internal helpers do not receive artificial public seams solely for mocking.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `providers, integration`

<a id="spec-td-05"></a>
- `spec-td-05` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 5
  Good tests assert semantic structure, page order, extracted values, layout breaks, geometry, rendered appearance, conformance findings, publication state, or stable errors. They do not assert PDFBox object identity, private method calls, internal batching details, temporary filenames, or byte ordering.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `integration, acceptance`

<a id="spec-td-06"></a>
- `spec-td-06` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 6
  Syntax evidence uses an external qpdf process and cannot alone prove standards compliance.
  Disposition: `required`. Unchanged Foundation requirement; all assigned obligations remain mandatory. Obligations: `acceptance`

<a id="spec-td-07"></a>
- `spec-td-07` — https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf/issues/1 — Testing Decisions 7
  PDF/A and machine-testable PDF/UA evidence uses an independently versioned veraPDF process with explicit flavour and recorded rule or clause findings.
  Disposition: `later-release`. Explicit later dependency-gated Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion or Sanitization work; not part of Foundation 0.1.0. Obligations: none
